app.name: Salesforce (Connected App / External Client App in your own org)

verdict.summary: Creating your own Salesforce OAuth app for your own org is a short console task, and Composio's managed Salesforce app lets you test first. Distribution beyond your own org (AppExchange or public install) is unverified: the official docs and partner review pages could not be read, so review scope and timing are unknown.
verdict.hands_on_effort: 30-60 min for your own app; review work for wider distribution is unknown
verdict.time_to_first_connection: 15-30 min after you have a Salesforce org with access to App Manager
verdict.approval_wait: none for your own org (Gate 1); wider distribution wait not verified

gates.name: Your own org (developer access)
gates.unlocks: Create the OAuth app in your own Salesforce org and connect your own account through Composio with your own Consumer Key and Secret.
limits: No review step was found for creating an app in your own org.
Exact account prerequisites for a Developer Edition or Partner org were not verified (official docs returned 403).

gates.name: Invited / test users (not verified)
gates.unlocks: Unknown from current research. Presumably other users in the same org can authorize the app, but this was not confirmed.
limits: User caps, install limits and token expiry for an unreviewed app were not found in the findings.
Whether Salesforce uses a test-user allowlist or similar mechanism was not verified.

gates.name: Anyone (AppExchange / AgentExchange listing)
gates.unlocks: Public distribution through the Salesforce partner listing path. Partner pages suggest an ISV track with Security Review, Technical Review, Sign Agreement and Sell on AppExchange items.
limits: The security-review page returned 404, so timeline, fees, artifacts and rejection reasons are unverified.
AppExchange branding now redirects to AgentExchange, so the listing path name may have changed.

steps.title: Decide between managed auth and your own app
steps.detail: Start with Composio's managed Salesforce OAuth to test the flow. Move to your own Salesforce app when you need your own branding, your own redirect URI, or distribution beyond Composio's shared app.
gotchas: Composio's shared app caps and whether its default redirect must be whitelisted were not verified.

steps.title: Get a Salesforce org you can administer
steps.detail: Sign up at the Salesforce developer signup page or use an existing org where you have admin access. You need access to Setup and App Manager.
gotchas: The signup and developer docs pages returned 403 to the research probe, so account prerequisites could not be confirmed.
Sign-up for a developer org may require identity verification. This was not checked.

steps.title: Create the connected app in Setup
steps.detail: In Salesforce, open Setup, then App Manager, and create a new connected app. Name it for your agent. Current Salesforce UI may steer new apps to External Client Apps rather than classic Connected Apps; this was not confirmed, so use whichever type your org offers and check the field labels.
gotchas: Classic Connected App vs. External Client App was not confirmed from a primary source.

steps.title: Enable OAuth Settings and set the Redirect URI
steps.detail: On the app, enable OAuth Settings and paste the callback URL from your Composio auth config into the callback URL field. Do not guess the URL; copy it from the Composio callout on this page.

values.label: Redirect URI
values.value: Composio callback URL (see the Composio callout on this page)

gotchas: Redirect URI rules (http vs https, localhost, wildcards) were not verified.

steps.title: Select OAuth scopes
steps.detail: Add the scopes Composio requests by default: full, refresh_token and openid. Add api, offline_access, id or web only if your use case needs them. Scope sensitivity labels were not verified.
gotchas: full grants broad access; keep only what the agent needs once you know your use case.

steps.title: Save and copy the Consumer Key and Secret
steps.detail: Save the connected app. Open the app detail page and copy the Consumer Key and Consumer Secret. Store the secret in your secrets manager, not in code.

values.label: Copy from
values.value: App detail page (Consumer Key and Consumer Secret)

gotchas: Consumer Secret handling and rotation rules were not verified.

steps.title: Enter the credentials in Composio
steps.detail: In Composio, create or edit the Salesforce auth config for your own app and paste the Consumer Key and Consumer Secret. Confirm the authorize and token URLs match the ones below.

values.label: Redirect URI
values.value: Composio callback URL (see the Composio callout on this page)

gotchas: Use the Composio callback URL shown in your own auth config, not the default shown in research, if they differ.

steps.title: Run a test authorization with your own account
steps.detail: Connect a Salesforce account through the Composio auth config and confirm the consent screen lists your scopes. Confirm the token exchange succeeds and an API call runs.
gotchas: Token expiry and refresh-token behaviour were not verified.

steps.title: Use PKCE if your client supports it
steps.detail: If you run your own OAuth client rather than relying only on Composio, use PKCE with the S256 challenge method. The discovery document advertises S256. Whether Salesforce enforces PKCE for your app was not verified.

steps.title: Draft app metadata and scope justifications
steps.detail: Draft the app description, a per-scope justification and a privacy-policy outline. Salesforce's legal pages are public and can be used as reference for privacy and terms links.
gotchas: Confirm what Salesforce requires for listings before using these drafts externally.

steps.title: Test with other users in the same org (Gate 2)
steps.detail: Ask another user in your org to authorize the app and confirm the flow works. Record any warning screens, user caps or expiry behaviour you see. Current Salesforce limits for unreviewed apps were not found.
gotchas: Gate 2 limits are unverified; do not promise invited-user caps to your users.

steps.title: Check the listing path before any AppExchange submission (Gate 3)
steps.detail: Before planning a public listing, confirm the current partner path in Salesforce's partner portal. Partner pages show an ISV track with Security Review and Sell on AppExchange items, but the security-review page returned 404 and AppExchange now points to AgentExchange.
gotchas: Do not assume a review timeline or fees until confirmed in the partner portal.

steps.title: Submit for review (Gate 3, only if you list publicly)
steps.detail: If you want a public listing, submit through the partner portal after you confirm the steps and artifacts. Public installs without a listing may not need review; this was not verified.
gotchas: Review artifacts, timeline and rejection reasons were not verified.

steps.title: Wait for provider review, if any
steps.detail: If a review applies, wait for Salesforce's decision. Do not plan a launch date until the timeline is confirmed.

requirements.detail: Needed to create the connected app. Prerequisites for a Developer Edition or Partner account were not verified.

requirements.detail: Partner navigation shows Security Review, Technical Review, Sign Agreement and Sell on AppExchange items. Their requirements were not verified.

blockers.symptom: Official Salesforce developer docs and signup pages return 403 to the research tool.
blockers.cause: Access restriction on developer.salesforce.com for the probe; not a confirmed developer-facing blocker.
blockers.fix: Open the developer signup and OAuth docs in a normal browser and confirm account prerequisites, redirect URI rules and token expiry before relying on this guide.

blockers.symptom: AppExchange security-review page returns 404; AppExchange branding redirects to AgentExchange.
blockers.cause: The listing path or name appears to have changed, so the review steps could not be read.
blockers.fix: Find the current listing and security-review path in the Salesforce partner portal before planning any public listing.

composio.note: Composio offers managed OAuth for Salesforce. Start with managed auth to test the flow. Create your own Salesforce Connected App (Consumer Key and Secret) only when you need your own branding, your own redirect URI, or distribution beyond Composio's shared app. Composio also lists an S2S_OAUTH2 mode with no default URLs; it needs separate setup and was not covered here.

evidence.claim: Composio catalog lists managed OAuth for Salesforce with default scopes full, refresh_token, openid and the login.salesforce.com authorize and token URLs.
evidence.quote: managed_oauth_available: true; default_scopes: full, refresh_token, openid

evidence.claim: Salesforce OIDC discovery at login.salesforce.com advertises the authorize and token endpoints, a revocation endpoint, and PKCE S256 support.
The discovery document lists scopes including full, api, refresh_token, offline_access, openid, id, web, chatter_api, and product-specific scopes.
evidence.quote: scopes_supported includes full, api, refresh_token, offline_access, openid

evidence.claim: The authorize endpoint probe was blocked, so invalid-client rejection behaviour was not observed.
evidence.quote: blocked: host is not a public internet host

evidence.claim: Community walkthrough: in Setup, App Manager, enable OAuth Settings, enter a callback URL, select OAuth scopes, save, then copy the Consumer Key and Secret.
evidence.quote: Setup > App Manager > Enable OAuth Settings > Choose Scopes and enter Callback URL.

evidence.claim: Salesforce's official developer docs and signup pages returned HTTP 403 to the probe tool, so official creation steps and redirect-URI rules could not be confirmed.
The Salesforce Help connected-app creation article URL resolves, but its content was not read.
Salesforce's partner site exposes an ISV navigation path with Security_Review, Technical_Review, Sign_Agreement and Sell_On_AppExchange items.
The specific security-review URL on the partner site returned 404, so its content was not retrieved.
The AppExchange domain now redirects its branding to AgentExchange, so the listing path name may have changed.
Salesforce's legal page is live with no login wall, useful for locating privacy and terms links.

open_questions: Official Salesforce developer docs returned 403, so account prerequisites, the exact creation UI, redirect URI rules (http vs https, localhost, wildcards), PKCE enforcement, token expiry and session policy are unverified.
Whether Salesforce now steers new apps to External Client Apps rather than classic Connected Apps is unconfirmed.
Scope sensitivity labels (restricted, privileged) were not retrieved; all scope tiers are marked unknown.
AppExchange / AgentExchange security review: steps, timeline, fees, artifacts, install caps and rejection reasons were not verified. The review page returned 404.
Whether Composio's shared Salesforce app has install or user caps, and whether its default redirect URI must be whitelisted in a custom app, was not checked.
Authorize endpoint invalid-client behaviour was not observed because the probe blocked login.salesforce.com.
Gate 2 caps (test users, dev-store-style limits, warning screens) were not found. Research relied mainly on Composio data and one discovery probe, plus one community walkthrough.
